subject: vLLM v0.28.0 release, GitHub tag v0.28.0, published 2026-08-26
central_claim: vLLM v0.28.0 is a publishable AI engineering topic because the official release note, GitHub tag, release API, source repository and public release artifacts support a bounded E2/R2 claim: the runtime release moves recent large MoE and long-context agent models such as Kimi-K3, DeepSeek V4 and Qwen3.8 from model-card compatibility into serving work on decode kernels, speculative decoding, KV cache tiering, hardware backends, API routing and security hardening, while project-reported speedups remain non-independent and workload-specific.

selection.reason: vLLM v0.28.0 was published on 2026-08-26 and had not been selected as a prior AI article. It is directly useful to engineers operating open and API-like model servers because it changes serving support for Kimi-K3, DeepSeek V4, Qwen3.8, speculative decoding, KV offload, ROCm/XPU/CUDA artifacts, API frontend behavior and security boundaries. Public evidence includes release notes, a GitHub tag/commit, release API metadata and downloadable artifacts. The conclusion is limited because this turn did not install vLLM or run GPU benchmarks.

claims.claim: vLLM v0.28.0 is best treated as a runtime release for serving the new class of large MoE, long-context and agent-oriented models, not as an independently proven universal speedup: the public release documents Kimi-K3 and DeepSeek V4 serving work, speculative decoding changes, KV tiering, hardware artifacts and API/security changes, while its speedup figures remain project-reported and condition-bound.

signals.note: Searched official or registry-first paths for OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, Qwen, DeepSeek, Mistral, Hugging Face Transformers, PyTorch, SGLang, vLLM and InferenceX. Search snippets, news snippets and social signals were used only to discover possible primary sources; article facts were not promoted without opened official release notes, model cards, GitHub releases, raw repository/API files or official documentation.

Opened OpenAI News and recent OpenAI posts around 2026-08-31, including ChatGPT Ads expansion, ChatGPT for Teachers expansion, Cursor contract wind-down, GPT-5.6 pages and Jalapeno posts. The 2026-08-31 items were product, education, company or advertising announcements with limited AI engineering artifact depth. Jalapeno was strong but already selected for the 2026-08-26 AI edition.

Opened Anthropic newsroom and release-note paths for Claude in Chrome, Claude Code on the web, release notes and Model Hardware Standard. The available late-August items were product availability or research-preview surfaces. Model Hardware Standard remained important but not open-sourced, and Claude browser/code product changes did not outrank the vLLM runtime release in public artifact depth.

Opened Gemini API changelog. Recent substantive items included Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash and prior Gemini 3.7/3.6 model changes. Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash was already handled for the 2026-08-30 AI edition and later visible entries were deprecation/product updates rather than a new non-duplicate model/runtime article.

Opened Qwen3.8-Flash-Next official blog/model card/GitHub paths, DeepSeek official Hugging Face registry paths and Z.ai GLM-5.3-Flash history. Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, DeepSeek V4-Pro and GLM-5.3-Flash are technically strong artifact-backed topics, but the relevant central claims were already covered by recent AI regular or special articles.

Opened Mistral changelog, PyTorch release notes, Hugging Face Transformers release paths, SGLang releases and vLLM releases. Mistral's visible model entries were older or not stronger than runtime candidates. PyTorch 2.13.0 is implementation-backed but old for this slot. Transformers releases followed already covered model support. SGLang v0.5.18 was useful but older and more diffuse. vLLM v0.28.0 was the strongest non-duplicate implementation-backed release found.

Opened vLLM v0.28.0 release note and release API. The release was published 2026-08-26T09:46:30Z, documents 584 commits from 270 contributors, lists Kimi-K3 and DeepSeek V4 serving work, speculative decoding, Model Runner V2 maturation, tiered KV cache offloading, Rust frontend/gRPC, hardware backend changes, API/security changes, breaking changes and release artifacts.

Fetched GitHub release API for vLLM v0.28.0. It returned 9 release assets including source tarball, CPU wheels, CUDA 12.9 wheels and XPU wheel with SHA-256 digests. The release note separately lists PyPI CUDA 13.0 install path, ROCm wheel index and Docker images for CUDA 13.0, CUDA 12.9, ROCm, CPU and XPU.

Searched content/ai, decisions/ai and var/runs/ai for vLLM v0.28.0, Kimi-K3 performance push, DeepSeek V4 sparse MLA, Jalapeno, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and related candidates. vLLM v0.28.0 appeared only as a non-selected alternative in the 2026-08-28 evidence, not as a published AI article. Jalapeno and Qwen3.8-Flash-Next were excluded as duplicates.

benchmark_notes.use_scope: Release-note speedup and memory-saving figures are used only to explain what the project claims changed and which workload dimensions matter. They are not used as an independent ranking or procurement conclusion.
reported_conditions: Kimi-K3 combined all-gathers are described as a 1.5~3x kernel-level speedup.
Adaptive speculative token budget is described as delivering about 60% better DSpark TTFT.
Optional shared-expert sharding is described as saving about 17 GiB of memory per GPU.
limitations: The article did not open and audit every linked PR or run a benchmark.
Release-note figures are condition-bound and may not carry to other models, hardware, concurrency or quantization settings.
